faq.title: Questions, answered
faq.intro: Can't find what you need? Send us a message.

items.q: How long does a typical project take?
items.a: A five-page site usually launches within two weeks of the plan being approved. Larger builds with custom automation take four to eight weeks.

items.q: Do you work with an existing website?
items.a: Yes. We can audit and improve what you have, migrate it safely, or rebuild only the parts that hold performance back.

items.q: Will I be able to edit content myself?
items.a: Content lives in simple text files or your preferred CMS. We document the workflow so your team can publish without a developer.

items.q: How do you measure SEO success?
items.a: We agree on a small set of metrics up front, such as qualified organic sessions, enquiries and ranking for priority pages, and report on them monthly.
Anything with an API or a webhook: forms, CRMs, spreadsheets, email platforms and messaging tools. We use n8n and custom scripts.

cta.title: Ready to build something that lasts?
cta.body: Tell us about your project. We reply within one business day with honest next steps.

services.title: Services
services.intro: Practical help for teams that want to be found, load fast and spend less time on repetitive work.
services.metaDescription: Technical SEO, web development, workflow automation and content strategy from Acme Digital.

items.name: Technical SEO
items.summary: Audits and fixes that help search engines crawl, understand and rank your pages.
items.description: We find what is holding your site back in search and fix it: crawl budget, indexation, internal links, structured data and Core Web Vitals. You receive a prioritised action list, and we can implement the changes with you.
deliverables: Prioritised fix list with effort estimates

faq.a: Technical fixes can show effects within weeks, but competitive terms usually take three to six months. We set realistic expectations before we begin.

faq.q: Do you need access to my analytics?
faq.a: Read-only access to Search Console and analytics helps us a lot, but we can start with a public crawl.

items.name: Web development
items.summary: Fast, accessible, maintainable websites built on modern tooling.
items.description: We design and build marketing sites and content platforms that are accessible, secure and quick on slow phones. Static generation, clean markup and typed code keep them cheap to host and easy to change.
deliverables: Static-first build with great Core Web Vitals

faq.a: Next.js, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS are our defaults, but we choose the simplest tool that meets the goal.

faq.q: Can you work with my designer?
faq.a: Absolutely. We can implement an existing design system or help shape one.

items.name: Workflow automation
items.summary: Connect forms, CRMs and reporting so routine tasks run by themselves.
items.description: We map the repetitive work in your week and automate it with webhooks, n8n and small custom scripts. Think lead routing, instant notifications, report generation and data clean-up, all signed, logged and easy to monitor.
deliverables: Process map of what to automate first
Runbook so your team can maintain them

faq.a: Requests are signed, secrets stay in environment variables and we only move the data each workflow needs.
Every workflow reports failures to a channel of your choice and retries safely where possible.

items.name: Content strategy
items.summary: Keyword research and editorial plans that attract the right readers.
items.description: We turn search demand into a content roadmap: topics, page types, internal linking and a publishing rhythm that your team can sustain. Briefs are written so any good writer can deliver them.

faq.a: We can, or we can brief your writers and edit their drafts. Whichever fits your budget.

faq.q: How many articles do we need?
faq.a: Fewer than you think. A focused set of strong pages usually beats a large number of thin ones.
